_note: The Grand Tour: Howdy, Stranger! Welcome series, one section per post (Todd, Nov 16 2026). head = the joke (card headline, under 60 chars), deck = plain facts on the card, body = caption facts. Facts drawn from the Nov 16 paper and Visitor Guide. No em-dashes.

stops.head: We Sit Through the Meetings So You Don't Have To
stops.deck: Council, Planning Commission and county decisions that reach Nevada City, in plain English, every morning.
stops.body: City Hall & Politics leads most mornings: what the City Council, Planning Commission and county supervisors are about to decide, and what they just did, with the dollar figures and the dates. Zoning, permits and new businesses are on the beat every day.
stops.alt: A cartoon newspaper reporter with a PRESS card in his hat, dozing in a chair at a council meeting

stops.head: All the Crime That's Fit to Print (Mostly Loose Dogs)
stops.deck: The Police Blotter: the week's calls to police and the sheriff, retold in our own words.
stops.body: The Police Blotter retells the latest calls to police and the sheriff in our own words: complaints about a neighbor's drumming, a tree crew that left its wood chips behind, and now and then something serious. Drawn from the published logs.
stops.alt: A cartoon beat cop blowing a whistle at a scruffy dog running off with a string of sausages

stops.head: Gossip? Heavens, No. Community News!
stops.deck: Here & There: food drives, water district news, closures, openings and the rest of what's going on around the county.
stops.body: Here & There rounds up the rest of the news around Nevada City and the county: food drives, water district business, openings and closings, and the things your neighbors will be talking about by lunch. Every item ends with its source.
stops.alt: A cartoon lady with red curls on a candlestick telephone, eyes wide at the latest news

stops.head: Bring an Umbrella, a Sweater, and Your Patience
stops.deck: Weather: the foothill forecast every morning. A big storm or a fire leads the paper.
stops.body: The Weather section gives the foothill forecast every morning: rain totals, frost, wind and Sierra watches. When a major storm or a fire is coming, it leads the paper under its own heading.
stops.alt: A cartoon fellow in a sweater and scarf whose umbrella has blown inside out in the rain

stops.head: Shake Hands With the Shopkeep!
stops.deck: Merchant of the Day: one Nevada City business profiled every morning. The Nugget picks them; no one pays to appear.
stops.body: Merchant of the Day profiles one Nevada City business each morning, with its address, hours and story. The Nugget picks them, and no one pays to appear. (Our publisher owns The Hat Store on Broad Street, and we say so.)
stops.alt: A cartoon shopkeeper with a handlebar mustache reaching across the counter to shake a customer's hand

stops.head: Tonight's Picture Show, Music Hall and Merriment
stops.deck: Amusements: Onyx showtimes, stage shows, live music and the KVMR radio log, every day.
stops.body: Amusements is the what-to-do-tonight page: showtimes at the Onyx, stage shows, live music around town and the day's KVMR radio log, plus a countdown to the big events.
stops.alt: A cartoon vaudeville hoofer in a straw boater kicking up a heel under the spotlight

stops.head: Grandpa's Newspaper Called. It Wants Its Headlines Back.
stops.deck: The Back Page: stories from the Nugget's morgue, the original paper's pages from the 1940s.
stops.body: The Back Page digs into the morgue: stories from the original Nevada City Nugget of the 1940s, retold, like the hometown woman who ran a Red Cross club in Germany for 8,000 soldiers a day.
stops.alt: A cartoon grandpa with spectacles and a white beard reading a 1945 newspaper in his rocking chair

stops.head: Every Word They Said. Yes, Every Word.
stops.deck: Meetings on the Record: searchable transcripts of City Council and Planning Commission meetings, each with a plain-English summary.
stops.body: Meetings on the Record has searchable transcripts of every City Council and Planning Commission meeting the city has posted since July, each opening with The Short of It, a plain-English summary. Tap a timestamp to jump to that moment in the city's video. Unofficial, machine-made from captions; the city's minutes are the record.
stops.alt: A cartoon stenographer pounding a typewriter as a long ribbon of transcript spools out

stops.head: Overheard at the Council Table
stops.deck: From the Dais: one quote a day from a council meeting, with a link to the moment on video.
stops.body: From the Dais is one quote a day from the people who run the city, straight from a council meeting, with the date and a link to that moment in the city's video.
stops.alt: A cartoon councilmember at the dais speaking into an old ribbon microphone, quote marks flying

stops.head: Read the Agenda Before the Agenda Reads You
stops.deck: The Docket: every council and planning agenda, digested item by item the morning after it posts. Downtown items are marked.
stops.body: The Docket digests every published City Council and Planning Commission agenda, item by item, the morning after it posts, and keeps it there until the meeting. Anything touching downtown or the commercial district gets a mark.
stops.alt: A cartoon clerk in spectacles gaping at an agenda scroll that unrolls all the way to the floor

stops.head: Mark Your Calendar, Sharpen Your Pencil
stops.deck: Civic Calendar for the week's public meetings and events, and Coming Attractions counting down the big ones.
stops.body: The Civic Calendar lists the week's public meetings and community events, day by day. Coming Attractions counts down the big ones: Thanksgiving weekend, Victorian Christmas, the Wild & Scenic Film Festival.
stops.alt: A cartoon pencil with a face and white gloves circling a date on a wall calendar

stops.head: Who's Running This Town, Anyhow?
stops.deck: Your Elected Officials: who sits on the council, and everything each has said on the record lately.
stops.body: Elected Officials names the mayor, vice mayor and council members, and the Officials' Page has profiles and everything each has said on the record lately.
stops.alt: A cartoon politician in a top hat and sash on a soapbox, hollering through a megaphone

stops.head: The Fine Print, Now in Larger Print
stops.deck: Legal Notices & Permits: planning applications, sign permits and hearings, posted as they open.
stops.body: Legal Notices & Permits lists what's open: planning applications, sign permits, architectural reviews and the hearings where you can speak up. New signs on Broad Street show up here first.
stops.alt: A cartoon town crier in a derby ringing a brass bell, with a HEAR YE notice scroll

stops.head: Dust Off Your Spurs, It's History Sunday
stops.deck: Local History Unearthed: a Sunday feature on Nevada City's past, plus Old West briefs now and then.
stops.body: Local History Unearthed runs Sundays: the old saloons of the downtown district and more of the town's past, plus occasional Old West briefs, like the lady who dealt twenty-one on Broad Street.
stops.alt: A cartoon cowpoke in a ten-gallon hat blowing a cloud of dust off an old history book

stops.head: Free to a Good Home: Love, Fur and Opinions
stops.deck: The Menagerie: Saturdays, adoptable animals from the county shelter plus the lost-and-found.
stops.body: The Menagerie runs Saturdays: adoptable animals from the county animal shelter and the lost-and-found form, for anyone missing a cat.
stops.alt: A cartoon puppy and kitten peeking out of a crate under a sign reading FREE TO A GOOD HOME

stops.head: Same Time Tomorrow? Swell!
stops.deck: A fresh paper every morning by 6, with a peek at tomorrow's at the end of each edition. Free by email too.
stops.body: A fresh Nugget comes out every morning by 6, and Tomorrow in the Nugget at the end of each edition tells you what's coming. Get it free by email, or put it on your phone's home screen.
stops.alt: A cartoon rooster crowing at sunrise atop a bundle of newspapers

stops.head: Breakfast, Lunch and Supper at Three Prices
stops.deck: Visitor Guide: The Bill of Fare picks where to eat today, at $, $$ and $$$.
stops.body: In the Nevada City Visitor Guide, The Bill of Fare picks where to eat each day, breakfast, lunch and dinner, at $, $$ and $$$, with hours for that day.
stops.alt: A cartoon waiter with a handlebar mustache and a towel on his arm lifting the cover off a dish

stops.head: Where Can I Get a Damn Drink Around Here?
stops.deck: The Bar Guide: saloons, cocktail lounges, brewpubs and tasting rooms, with hours and a little saloon history.
stops.body: Our most-asked question has a whole guide: saloons and late bars, cocktail lounges, brewpubs, tasting rooms and the roadhouse out on Highway 49, with hours as each posts them, most a short walk from Broad Street. Plus a history of the old saloons. Please drink responsibly.
stops.alt: A cartoon bartender with sleeve garters sliding a foaming mug down the bar

stops.head: Lace Up! The Hills Ain't Gonna Climb Themselves
stops.deck: Trails & Vistas: a Trail of the Day with distance, climb and directions, plus the full guide.
stops.body: Trails & Vistas picks a Trail of the Day, with its distance, climb, surface and how to get there, like the nearly level Cascade Canal Trail on Banner Mountain. The full guide covers the rest.
stops.alt: A cartoon hiker with a walking stick, a big pack and red boots striding up a pine-covered ridge

stops.head: There's More to Town Than Broad Street, Pardner
stops.deck: Spotlight on Seven Hills: Nevada City's other business district, off Zion Street.
stops.body: A mile south of Broad Street, off Zion Street, the Seven Hills District is where Nevada City runs its errands, with an arthouse theater, food shops and places to eat. The Visitor Guide's Spotlight shows you around.
stops.alt: A cartoon traveler with a bindle pointing past street signs for Zion Street, Broad Street and Seven Hills

stops.head: A Bed for the Night and a Map for the Morning
stops.deck: Where to Stay: historic hotels, inns and campgrounds. Day Trips from Sacramento and Truckee.
stops.body: Getting Here & Staying Over: Where to Stay lists the historic hotels, inns, cottages and campgrounds, and the Day Trips guides plan a visit from Sacramento (about 1.5 hours) or Truckee (about 45 minutes).
stops.alt: A cartoon fellow in a nightcap yawning in bed with a candle, the moon and stars outside

stops.head: Book Early, Gloat Later
stops.deck: Plan Ahead: the big events worth booking a bed for, with dates and links.
stops.body: Plan Ahead in the Visitor Guide flags the big events worth booking ahead for, like the Wild & Scenic Film Festival, Feb. 18 to 22, 2027, when festival weekend fills the town.
stops.alt: A cartoon traveler in a fedora checking his pocket watch beside a suitcase plastered with stickers
